examples: 1980s–90s Pioneer / Sony / Blaupunkt / Clarion cassette decks
OEM cassette units from the same era
one_liner: A wide flat face where the cassette door was, and nothing inside that can hurt you.

price.why: Nobody wants these at all, which is the point.

window_w_mm.why: There is usually no display window worth using — the space is the cassette door. That is an OPPORTUNITY: a flat rectangular hole you can cut cleanly, rather than a small one you must enlarge.

chassis.why: Built like furniture. Also the deepest chassis here, which is the wrong direction if your car is tight.

cage_included.v: sometimes; older units were often screwed in directly
cage_included.why: ⚠️ Pre-ISO mounting is common on this era. Budget for a new cage.

buttons.v: mechanical, large, satisfying, and often not on a flexi
buttons.why: Discrete switches are EASIER to convert to a ladder than a matrix, not harder.

knob.v: often twin concentric knobs — volume and tone
knob.why: The best-feeling knobs of any donor here, by a wide margin.

display_tech.v: none, or a small backlit dial
display_tech.why: Nothing to discharge. The safest possible teardown.

why: The cassette aperture is a big, clean, rectangular hole in the middle of the face — which is exactly the shape the deck's panel wants, and you are cutting an existing opening rather than making one.
No laser, no inverter, nothing charged. The safest category.
The knobs and buttons are the nicest to use, and period-correct for the aesthetic this whole project is chasing.
watch_out: Depth. These are the deepest chassis in this document.
⚠️ Pre-ISO mounting on the older ones — the cage may not be a cage. Check before assuming it drops into a modern aperture.
The fascia is often painted rather than moulded, and paint from 1988 does not survive being worked on.
steps: Remove the cassette mechanism — it is usually one sub-assembly on four screws and comes out whole.
The cassette aperture becomes the window. Back it with 1 mm smoked acrylic bonded from behind and it looks like it was always a display.
Convert the discrete switches to the ladder directly — no flexi to lift, just a wire per switch and a common return.
⚠️ Check the mounting before you build the chassis: if it is pre-ISO you need a modern cage and the donor's own brackets are no use.
